en: Mayon Volcano erupts because the Philippine Sea Plate subducts under the Eurasian Plate, melting rock into magma that rises to the surface.
The Pasig River flows into Manila Bay because gravity pulls freshwater from Laguna de Bay down the elevation gradient toward the ocean.
Typhoons gain strength over the warm Philippine Sea because the heated ocean water evaporates rapidly, providing the energy and moisture needed to fuel the storm.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River formed because slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the soluble limestone bedrock of the St. Paul Mountain Range over millions of years.
The Banaue Rice Terraces prevent soil erosion because the carved stone walls and flooded paddies slow down rainwater runoff on the steep Cordillera mountains.
Tubbataha Reef supports diverse marine life because its shallow, clear waters allow sunlight to penetrate, enabling symbiotic algae inside corals to photosynthesize and grow.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant generates electricity because steam from underground volcanic reservoirs in Albay is piped up to spin turbines connected to generators.
The Sierra Madre mountains cause heavy rainfall on their eastern side because they force moisture-laden typhoon winds upward, cooling the air and condensing the moisture.
Lake Taal exists inside a volcanic crater because a massive ancient eruption emptied the underlying magma chamber, causing the ground above it to collapse inward.
The volcanic soil in Bukidnon is highly fertile because weathered ash and lava from past eruptions release essential minerals like potassium into the earth.
Mangrove forests in the Sulu Sea prevent coastal erosion because their dense, tangled root systems trap sediments and physically break the energy of incoming waves.
Strong tidal currents flow through the San Juanico Strait because the narrow channel squeezes the massive volume of water moving between the Samar and Leyte gulfs.
